question: When was Bharatanatyam banned by the British colonial government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1910**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 1910 is the year when Bharatanatyam was banned by the British colonial government.
 
• The ban was part of the British policy to suppress Indian traditions and cultures.
 
• Bharatanatyam was seen as a vital expression of South Indian culture and spirituality.
 
• The ban led to the decline of temple dances and adversely affected the livelihoods of dancers.
 
• Efforts by Indian nationalists and revivalists in the 20th century helped to lift the ban and restore the dance form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
Aspect

 
 
 
Details

 
 
 

 
 
Origin

 
 
 
Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, India.

 
 
 

 
 
Elements

 
 
 
It includes nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance), and natya (dramatic storytelling).

 
 
 

 
 
Significance

 
 
 
It is not just an art form but a way to express devotion and spirituality.

 
 
 

 
 
Revival

 
 
 
The dance form saw a significant revival and restructuring in the 20th century, making it popular worldwide.

 
 
 

 
 
Cultural Impact

 
 
 
Bharatanatyam has played a crucial role in promoting Indian culture and heritage globally.
